newsitem.title: FRANCE: Warner has option on Canalsatellite - source.
newsitem.headline: Warner has option on Canalsatellite - source.

text.p: Warner Bros has an option to buy 10 percent of CanalSatellite, the satellite television unit of France's Canal Plus, a source close to the talks said on Monday.
However, Warner Bros had not signed up to have its television channels carried on CanalSatellite's digital service, the source said.
A Canal Plus spokeswoman declined comment.
Monday's edition of the financial daily La Tribune said Warner would announce plans to take 10 percent of CanalSatellite's digital service for between 500 million and 800 million francs.
CanalSatellite is owned 70 percent by Canal Plus, 10 percent by Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) and 20 percent by Pathe.
Warner Bros has been "Canal Plus's historic partner since the first purchases of broadcasting rights in 1983," the source said.
CGE said it wanted to sell its 10 percent of CanalSatellite when it announced in February a deal with Havas and Canal Plus to rationalise its communications and broadcasting interests.

As part of this rationalisation, the utilities and communications giant is in talks with Time Warner over the sale of its cable television networks unit, Compagnie Generale de Videocommunication (CGV), which made losses of some 300 million francs in 1996.
CGV is 71.6 percent-owned by CGE and 20 percent by Canal Plus.
La Tribune also said Warner would acquire CGV as part of the deal over CanalSatellite.
